title: SC settling to OTA spec
description: The classic switched-capacitor settling flow (Murmann): it turns a settling-time and error budget into the open-loop OTA requirements a downstream amplifier sheet must meet, then sizes one input device so the flow ends in silicon. The dynamic settling error sets the number of time constants; the clock period (half of it available for settling) sets the maximum closed-loop time constant; from those come the required unity-gain frequency GBW_req, the required DC gain $A_{req}$ (from the static error), and the required slew rate SR_req (from the large-signal step). GBW_req, $A_{req}$, and SR_req are surfaced as rows for a downstream OTA sheet to adopt as its GBW_target, $A_{v,target}$, and SR_target. Assumes a single-pole closed loop and a feedback factor $\beta$ (typically $C_f/(C_s+C_f)$); the slew/linear-settling boundary and phase margin are sim-owned.

params.name: T_s
params.note: full clock period; only half is available for settling (the other half samples)

params.name: eps_s
params.note: static settling error: 1/(loop gain), sets the required DC gain

params.name: eps_d
params.note: dynamic settling error: the residue after linear settling, sets the number of time constants

params.name: beta
params.note: feedback factor; typically Cf/(Cs+Cf) for an SC gain stage

params.name: V_step
params.note: output large-signal step, sets the slew requirement

params.name: t_slew_frac
params.note: fraction of the half-period allotted to slewing before linear settling begins

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion knob: high = efficient/slow, low = fast/thirsty

params.name: vds_in
params.note: input device drain bias (the output DC level), signed to the table axis

params.name: ft_margin
params.note: how many times faster than GBW_req the sized device must be

doc.title: SC input device
doc.description: One input device sized so the OTA's open-loop unity-gain frequency equals GBW_req into the effective load. gm is pinned from the settling flow; gm/ID is the efficiency knob.

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data

rows.name: N_tau
rows.note: time constants of linear settling to the dynamic error eps_d

rows.name: tau_max
rows.note: max closed-loop time constant: half the clock period divided by N_tau

rows.name: GBW_req
rows.note: required open-loop unity-gain frequency; single-pole closed-loop tau = 1/(2*pi*beta*GBW)

rows.name: A_req
rows.note: required open-loop DC gain: loop gain beta*A_req = 1/eps_s

rows.name: CL_eff
rows.note: effective output load during amplification: CL plus the series Cs-Cf combination

rows.name: SR_req
rows.note: required slew rate: the output step completed within the slewing portion of the half-period; estimate, the slew/linear boundary is sim-owned

rows.name: ft_in
rows.note: sized device transit frequency from its own gate cap

rules.note: the sized device's fT must clear GBW_req with margin; a real derived check (the pinned gm hid the gate cap), estimate-grade, sim signs off
